Is_Archiving_Enabled.description: FILESHARE_ARCHIVE_FOLDER is deliberately empty by default (see infra params) until a real path is confirmed for an environment - prod as of this writing has no confirmed archive path (its file share root is an entirely different share from dev's). This subflow safely no-ops rather than failing when archiving isn't configured, so wf-copy-invoices can call it unconditionally in every environment.

Copy_To_Archive.description: REST shape (POST /datasets/default/copyFile, source/destination/overwrite as query params) confirmed live against the real connector, 2026-08-14 - a throwaway test against an existing, already-processed disposable fixture (TestInvoice_Word_4.docx) returned a clean, specific 403 ('credentials for this connection do not have access to /Archive') rather than a malformed-request error, proving the request reached the actual file-system backend and was evaluated on permissions, not rejected as badly formed. Currently blocked by an external file-share ACL, not by this action's shape - see docs/operations/known-issues.md. overwrite=true per user decision (2026-08-14): a same-named file already in Archive gets overwritten, not uniquified or treated as a failure.

Delete_Source_After_Archive.description: REST shape NOT yet empirically confirmed (Copy_To_Archive fails first on the current permission blocker, so this action has never actually executed live) - best-effort guess following this connector's established by-id convention (GetFileContent's 'id' parameter accepts an encoded path directly, same as this). Only runs if Copy_To_Archive succeeded - never delete the source until the archive copy is confirmed to exist, so a failed/partial archive never loses the file entirely.

Response.description: Always returns 200 regardless of archive outcome - archiving is a best-effort, secondary step. The file's Succeeded status in ProcessedFiles is already written by the caller BEFORE this subflow is invoked, and must never be affected by whether the archive-move itself succeeds or fails.
